text:
Run the dry run first: `git clean -ndx`

It lists every untracked and ignored file and directory that would be deleted, and removes nothing.

Deletion cannot be undone: `git clean` bypasses the trash, and git does not track these files, so there is no recovery. Ignored files often include `.env` files, local config, and credentials.

Once you have checked the dry-run list, reply "confirm delete". The command is `git clean -fdx`.

claims.instrument: pattern check (no material bound: a model reading of specifics could only list them)

latitude.tightenedBy: Delete every untracked file in my repository right now, including ignored files.

acceptedUnmeasured.statement: Lead with the next action: the first line is something the reader can do, and a command, path, or snippet goes first with prose after, if at all.
End with one concrete next action the reader can do in under two minutes.

Finish the first issue, then offer the second as a separate question rather than mixing it in; answer mid-work questions yourself if you can, and if one still needs the reader, surface it once at the end.
Restate the current state every turn, e.g. which step is done and what is next, and use the harness's task or plan tool for multi-step work instead of also narrating the plan as prose.
Show what now works in concrete terms, with how to try it, instead of burying wins in a recap.

Keep these rules on for every response for the rest of the session, even when the topic changes, and turn them off only when the reader says "stop adhd mode" or "normal mode" (confirm in one line, then return to default style).

certificate.why: no delivered-error bound: it needs an audit sample of your own labels, drawn like the work this skill does; the checks and readers above are what this output was held to
